catalog_quote: [Hertsens 1940: 271, Northern Lendu, diacritics stripped] Dans cette etude nous ne parlerons que du groupe nord, nos etudes ayant eu trait principalement a ce groupe. Que le mot ‘ lendu ’ dans cette etude soit done toujours pris dans le sens ‘ lendu-nord ’. Le lendu est une langue isolante a caracteristiques soudanaises-est; mots strictement monosyllabiques, absence d’inflexions (incluant absence de genre grammatical et de systeme de classes); le genitif est place avant le mot qui le gouverne; langue a tonemes (les tons ont une valeur semantique et grammaticale). [Tucker & Bryan 1966, ch. 1 sec. 2a-2b, archive.org full-text highlights (snippet grade)] ... (MORU, MA’DI, LOGO, LUGBARA) and in LENDU, three tone levels have been established ... In LENDU only two Tone Classes have as yet been found ... 2b. Stress Larochette reports a tendency towards stress on the penultimate syllable of a word or phrase in MANGBETU, accompanied sometimes by extra high tone as in neka- *kidri, headache. No such uniformity of stress pattern, however, has been found in the other Language Groups. Even such intimately closely allied languages as MORU and MA’DI have quite different stress behaviour. In MORU stress is on the first syllable of disyllabic words, even when it is a vowel Prefix, e.g. 'iza, meat ... In MA’DI, however, stress is on the final vowel ... In both languages words within a phrase retain their original stress. ... LENDU apparently has only monosyllabic ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lendu is described as a tone language with three established tone levels; on stress the source says only that no uniform (predictable) stress pattern was found for the LENDU group (or for MORU-MA'DI and MANGBUTU-EFE), in contrast to the penultimate tendency reported for Mangbetu. No Lendu word is cited and no placement rule is given; this cannot be read as fixed, weight-sensitive or lexical stress -- only as 'no uniform pattern found'.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Lendu; the same section gives Moru initial stress ('iza) versus Ma'di final stress (i'za) as the contrasting cases, and notes that in both 'words within a phrase retain their original stress'.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level statement covering the whole LENDU group (chapter examples are from Northern Lendu = Bbadha, lend1245); word-level ('stress pattern'); text reconstructed from Open Library full-text search snippets of an access-restricted scan (scanned as indexed), so wording is reliable but page number is inferred. The open, saved primary phonology sources (Trifkovic 1977a, 1977b) are silent on stress and describe 3-4 level tones plus a rising contour.
new_statements.identity_note: All material concerns Lendu proper / Northern Lendu (Bbadha, Kilendu; lend1245). Tucker & Bryan 1966 state their LENDU examples are 'from N. LENDU unless otherwise indicated'. Hertsens 1940 splits 'le lendu ou ba dha' into a northern group (dialects north of 1°35'N) and a southern group 'parlés au pays de Géty' -- the latter is Ngiti (ngit1239, Glottolog's separate language), so any statement in Hertsens must be checked for which group it covers. Dhejju 1977 describes the Tadha dialect; Trifkovic 1977 does not name a dialect (informants M. Njabu, husband and wife; 'North Eastern Zaire').

Positions de thèses d'École de l'année 1978-1979 et positions de thèses de IIIe cycle, pp. 10-12. Paris: EPHE.
tone_statements.quote: Le segment de la syllabe lendu est toujours porteur d'un ton; ce segment est : soit, l'une des huit voyelles de la langue [i, e, s, a, o, o, u, w], soit, l'une des trois consonnes alvéolaires : [s, z, r]. [...] Le lendu distingue 4 tons phonologiques, dont trois tons ponctuels et un modulé montant. Ex. : /îlo/« chair »;/nô/« termite (sp.) »;/nô/« nourriture »;/nô/« œil, yeux ».
tone_statements.translation: The segment of the Lendu syllable always carries a tone; this segment is either one of the eight vowels of the language [i, e, ɛ, a, ɔ, o, u, ɨ(?)] or one of the three alveolar consonants [s, z, r]. [...] Lendu distinguishes 4 phonological tones, three level tones and one rising contour. E.g. /ilo/ 'flesh'; /no/ 'termite sp.'; /no/ 'food'; /no/ 'eye, eyes' (tone marks not recoverable from the scanned).
tone_statements.locator: p. 11, phonology paragraph of the thesis position; p. 10 carries the remarks on Tucker and Trifkovic
